audit.summary: The checked ground-state coercivity and conservative rescaling algebra support their uses. The noise probability argument requires divergence of the imaginary component; arbitrary growth of complex modulus does not give its claimed auxiliary limit. The final theorem is not refuted.

proposition.claim:
Recorded check: The nonconservative component, not merely complex modulus, must diverge in the probability step

T=1 fixed. X0(x)=exp(-|x|^2) is deterministic H1(R3); its squared H1 norm is 4*(pi/2)^(3/2). Y0=0 in L2(R3). phi_1^(1)=n+i is spatially constant with Im=1 nonzero. all first-noise modes k>=2 vanish. W2=0. real Brownian motion beta. the special noise assumptions of Theorem 1.7 replace conservative hypothesis (H). C3 is finite, positive, deterministic and depends only on fixed T and initial-data norms.
